| | Peter,

This week is National Agriculture Week, and for me, this one is personal.

I’m a timber and soybean farmer. I was raised on a cattle farm. My family has worked Arkansas land for generations, and today, we still do.

So when I talk about agriculture, I’m not talking about theory. **I’m talking about my family’s way of life.**

China has reopened its market to American soybeans, and that’s good news. Our farmers need strong markets and fair access.

**But I’m not going to pretend that everything is fine.**

For years, China has been investing in Brazil and building up their supply chain so they don’t have to rely on American farmers. That creates long-term uncertainty for folks right here in Arkansas.

And under the Biden Administration, we became dependent on China for used cooking oil, something our soybean farmers can produce right here at home. _That doesn’t make sense._

Here in Arkansas, we took action. We kicked China off our farmland.

**Our homeland belongs to Arkansans, not foreign adversaries.**

Here’s where I stand.
* _We should be growing markets for our farmers here at home._
* _We should be investing in soy-based biodiesel._
* _We should be strengthening American agriculture,**not** outsourcing it._

That’s how we support our farmers, strengthen our economy, and move toward real energy independence.

**I’ll _always_ stand up for Arkansas farmers.**

If you’re with me, I’m asking you to step up today.

Friend,

You’ve probably seen the reporting about Rick Jackson’s company using visa programs to import foreign nurses into Georgia hospitals. While our own nurses are stretched thin and families are paying more than ever for care, his business is leaning on foreign labor instead of building up a strong Georgia workforce.

[ ](http://links.burtjonesforga.com/u/click?_t=858b83d5086141569cc77db3b7b1b605&_m=4be0f3eaf3774bcdace46d3820fb2e3e&_e=D6qu6zzvg02lhZh2iFlPX33JlC1YlUV6GiuEi7qnKzAAwB_hYzk0xs465VA7FiYGSj1gvW3VR-HAd1RjssPOV3wKZupWSpOl-KIkFqkudcwkD3wOxHRhAOapoR8qLJ54BtrotZxGN2Ptz0t52guxAMjm7OFs3vFMG7Ew0sSqKgIdAufNRRPFC_A9SZZTNHCWF9Lc7pOKcJe4oCxfuKZlqzIGaQ7TMl4pboZukzKjsuBd45As7uaXSZkTRcXMqT_0Cn79_s3RZVtdDYcS3_MG1FJuT6_HAfTDQJEeGFUvgj0OVSmySEGHq-FKrPicju_Twx6rkJ1V6jpyeFdVl1oS7Ax6hVTqADIjMkyr_vyzDLY01Qt4DQytaZ6bLuvoBwVIDM67OlsuzTwj41JmufmROE2A1JSfK5O2R2Sc_L8viGJLGQCgLjSYapWOgoPD06bsfougDYlwjkOB_JLKd0eMLOcZTqydexiXafvPWoj8GnABcqsrt1hyzcpoF0sCztgZNfAY-s5kHMCQLZbNN7a-Wm3HUPGSPqTbPAFyDTPeYuU%3D)

That might help a billionaire CEO’s bottom line... but it’s not conservative Georgia values. Republicans are supposed to put American workers first, secure our borders, and stand up to the globalist mindset that treats cheap foreign labor as the answer to every problem.

My record is the opposite. I’ve fought to cut taxes, grow jobs here at home, back law enforcement – and I’m the only candidate for governor with President Trump’s full endorsement because I’ve stood with him from the start.

This primary comes down to a clear choice:

A Trump-endorsed, tested conservative who’s worked to create Georgia jobs and protect our communities. Or a billionaire whose healthcare empire relies on importing foreign nurses while claiming to be a tough-on-immigration “outsider.”

I’m in this race to fight for Georgia nurses, Georgia workers, and Georgia families – not the special interests that profit from shipping in foreign labor. But I can’t do it without you.

Here’s how you can help today:
* Forward this email to 5 conservative friends.
* Talk about this issue at church, work, and in your neighborhood.

Georgia is Trump Country, and with your help, we’re going to keep it that way.

Burt

P.S. When folks ask about this race, tell them: if you want a governor who puts Georgia workers first and stands with President Trump, we need your vote in this Republican primary.

From bill to emergency order: The election fight moves beyond Congress
| | | | [](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
---
**PRESENTED BY[ROCKYMOUNTAINVOICE.COM](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
| | Hi friends,
Listen to the Mountain Minute podcast [here](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.), or watch on [YouTube](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) or [Rumble](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.). And also, check out our [deep-dive video of the day](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) on the SAVE America Act and a new route being proposed if it doesn't pass.
Here is a summary of today's top stories:
🏛️ **Under the Golden Dome...** Democrats are advancing a measure that could [let the state retain TABOR refunds](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) in the name of "education funding"—estimated at about $817 million in its first year—pending voter approval in 2026, while lawmakers also debate an energy bill allowing large users to [build private power systems](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.), reflecting a broader clash over costs and regulation.

🏔️ **Here in Colorado...** [Opioid deaths are rising](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)—up 17% since late 2024—diverging from national declines, while the state’s wolf program faces scrutiny after a [44% survival rate among relocated animals](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.). A [strike at the JBS beef plant](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) in Greeley could impact supply if prolonged, as [debate continues](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) over the case of former clerk Tina Peters.
🇺🇸**On the National Stage...** Election integrity concerns are intensifying after reports of [offsite ballot handling in Arizona](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) and disclosures that [China accessed U.S. voter data](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) in 2020. Senate Republicans are pushing the SAVE Act requiring proof of citizenship, while some advocate for a [presidential emergency order to overhaul election rules](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.), as tensions involving Iran, Israel, and the U.S. continue to escalate.
This is your Mountain Minute for Wednesday, March 18, 2026.
– Team RMV
---
|
---
**TODAY'S TOP STORIES**
**[From bill to emergency order: The election fight moves beyond Congress](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** BY JEN SCHUMANN, [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
[](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
Senate Republicans opened debate Tuesday on a bill they say will secure American elections. But inside that same fight, a second path is already taking shape—one that doesn’t run through Congress at all.

While lawmakers argue over the SAVE America Act and whether it can survive a Senate filibuster, some election-integrity advocates are pushing something far more aggressive: a proposed emergency order that would allow a president to step in and change how federal elections are run.

RMV obtained a copy of that proposal—and spoke with one of the men now advocating for it. What’s emerging is not just a policy disagreement. It’s a split in approach. Congress is trying to answer the question through legislation. Others are asking whether a president should act now—without waiting for it.
**[READ MORE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
|
---
**[Framed as education, but tied to TABOR: Measure to keep surplus revenue advances](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** BY SHAINA COLE, [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
* **TABOR refund measure advances toward 2026 ballot:** Senate Bill 26-135 would let voters decide whether the state can keep revenue above TABOR limits instead of issuing refunds, with the Senate Finance Committee approving the measure on a 6–3 vote.
* **Plan could redirect hundreds of millions away from taxpayers:** The proposal is projected to retain about $817 million in its first year, with some funds allocated to education and property tax reimbursements, while remaining dollars could be spent on other state priorities.
* **Critics warn it expands spending beyond education:** Opponents argue the bill is framed as school funding but could permanently increase government spending and reduce future TABOR refunds, with fewer long-term limits on how the money is used.

**[READ MORE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**

**[Two visions of Colorado’s energy future collide in committee hearing](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** BY JEN SCHUMANN, [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
* **Energy bill highlights divide over Colorado’s power future:** Lawmakers clashed over House Bill 26-1246, with debate centered on whether new large electricity users should operate within the existing regulated grid or be allowed to build independent power systems.
* **Supporters argue plan protects ratepayers and land:** Backers say allowing large users to self-generate power would prevent infrastructure costs from being passed to households, reduce the need for new transmission lines across private land, and address rapidly growing electricity demand.
* **Opponents warn of reduced oversight and policy conflicts:** Critics argue the approach could weaken regulatory protections, shift costs to remaining customers, and conflict with Colorado’s broader energy and emissions goals if major users operate outside the system.

body:

Hi Peter,
With just over one week until our annual Roosevelt Dinner Awards, there is still time to buy a ticket if you haven't already!
Tickets Available! [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/roo27fed]
This year, we will be honoring the work of six extraordinary Democrats whose commitment to our shared values has led them to go above and beyond for our Commonwealth and our Party.
It is our great privilege to present the Roosevelt Award to Senate President Karen Spilka and Beth Boland, in recognition of their outstanding leadership and unwavering commitment to public service.
We will also solemnly honor the enduring legacy of State Representative Ann-Margaret Ferrante and The Honorable Setti Warren, presenting the Roosevelt Award in memory of their extraordinary life’s work and lasting contributions.
In addition, we are proud to recognize Jessica Tang, President of the American Federation of Teachers Massachusetts, with the Edward M. Kennedy “Lion of Labor” Award, celebrating her powerful advocacy and steadfast dedication to workers' rights.
Finally, we are delighted to honor Minnah Sheikh with the Christopher Condon Activist Award, recognizing her bold grassroots leadership and tireless efforts to uplift underrepresented communities.
We hope you’ll join us as we celebrate these exceptional honorees and their inspiring achievements. We look forward to sharing this special occasion with you.
Thank you,
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/NGP/NGP31/1/93809/images/Steve%20K%27s%20Signature.png]
Steve Kerrigan

name: KAREN CRNKOVICH FOR JOHNSON COUNTY COMMISSION
subject: The American Dream shouldn’t begin at 40
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY KAREN CRNKOVICH FOR JOHNSON COUNTY COMMISSION * 6709 West 119th Street * Ste
body:
Here’s how we can fix the housing affordability crisis...

| | | | | |
---
| |

Peter, My father was a traveling salesman. As a child, my family moved multiple times, every couple of years, I had to start over - a new city, a new school, and new friends. These experiences taught me two important lessons: resilience and the ability to make friends fast.
When I moved to Johnson County in 2004, I was ready to plant roots, and I immediately knew I had finally found the place to call home. A few years later, I was fortunate enough to buy my first home. I was 33 years old.Today, the average age of a first-time homebuyer is 40 years old. That makes the path to building wealth and achieving long-term stability difficult for families and hardworking individuals.Unfortunately, much of the affordability “crisis” is out of our control, including:
* Interest rates
* Supply and demand
* The cost of land and building materials

But let’s talk about what we _can_ control, because I see two major opportunities.First, we can ease the burden of arduous zoning rules and regulations, which fall squarely on Johnson County officials. Cutting red tape can lower costs for builders and make new homes more attainable for families.Second, rising property taxes are a major factor in the affordability struggle. When taxes climb year after year, staying in your home becomes harder, and buying one becomes even more daunting.**So, how do we, as everyday citizens, make meaningful change on these two fronts?****We elect the right people.****By supporting my campaign, you are supporting THE candidate who is a fiscally minded small business owner. I won’t pass the blame, and I won’t raise taxes to pursue a bloated budget.**
Mike Kelly and his “blank-check, big government” machine want to hold on to power. Why wouldn’t he? This allows him to push forward his personal agendas and pet projects at the cost of the taxpayers. To stop him - **I need help. Please consider joining my campaign as a volunteer; there is a role for anyone ready and able to be on the side of positive change.**

---
| [JOIN KC FOR JOCO](https://kcforjoco.us20.list-manage.com/track/click?u=d540da3225ec5b2797f3018d2&id=37819a5ae8&e=7320325a61)
---
| |

Johnson County should be a place where families can grow, and young people can buy their first home, and I’m committed to finding balanced, practical solutions to make that happen - let’s do this together!Sincerely,Karen Crnkovich
Candidate for Johnson County Commission ChairP.S. I've discussed this topic in several videos over on Facebook. [If you aren’t following me, head over there and let me know what you think. ](https://kcforjoco.us20.list-manage.com/track/click?u=d540da3225ec5b2797f3018d2&id=9d5e89cc66&e=7320325a61)
Thank you,Karen Crnkovich

body:
Individual actions become unstoppable when we come together.

| [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/127589194/608567889/1328794144?refcode=ea.bb18c3ba-0123-f111-9a48-000d3a14b640&ms=ea.bb18c3ba-0123-f111-9a48-000d3a14b640&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9FQS9FQTAxNi8xLzk2NzgyIiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogImJiMThjM2JhLTAxMjMtZjExMS05YTQ4LTAwMGQzYTE0YjY0MCIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=hWZnajF7P8Ro0ghwK7IevxeypW8jx2IzaTWoYcvqCco=&emci=d81858c3-e622-f111-9a48-000d3a14b640&emdi=bb18c3ba-0123-f111-9a48-000d3a14b640&ceid=4823105)
---
Everywhere we look, the consequences of burning planet-warming fossil fuels are staring us in the face. Severe winter storms. Record-breaking heat. Unrelenting wildfires. Floods, droughts, hurricanes — disasters that once felt “once in a lifetime” are now happening every month. And while some people would rather stop talking about climate altogether, I refuse to. We only have one planet, and protecting it will take all of us rolling up our sleeves and standing together to defend our air, our water, our communities, and the places we call home. **There is one thing that unites and undergirds everything this regime is doing, all the wars, and the destruction of our planet: Fossil fuels.** Reading this message, you may wonder: _What difference can one person really make?_ But here's what I've learned in my decades of activism: Individual actions, when multiplied across thousands of people, become a force that no one can ignore. That collective power is how change has _always_ happened, and it’s why I want to share something concrete and actionable today. I love these 10 suggestions from the David Suzuki Foundation for what each of us can do to shrink our footprint and save our planet. For those who don’t recognize Suzuki’s name, he is a beloved Canadian scientist and environmentalist who has written more than 50 books and inspired generations to care for our planet. | **10 powerful ways each of us can reduce our environmental impact and drive climate progress:**
1. Urge government to take bold, ambitious climate action now.

2. Use energy wisely — and save money too!

3. Get charged up with renewables.

4. Eat for a climate-stable planet.

5. Start a climate conversation.

6. Green your commute.

7. Consume less, waste less, enjoy life more.

8. Invest in renewables and divest from fossil fuels.

9. Mobilize for local climate action.

10. Get politically active and VOTE.

---
**So here's my ask: Take a moment to really consider these ten actions and pick three that you're ready to commit to. It could be something you're already doing that you want to do more intentionally, or it could be something completely new that challenges you to go further.**
**[Then join me in taking the climate pledge and make those three actions your commitment. clean_body: Individual actions become unstoppable when we come together. | Everywhere we look, the consequences of burning planet-warming fossil fuels are staring us in the face. Severe winter storms. Record-breaking heat. Unrelenting wildfires. Floods, droughts, hurricanes — disasters that once felt “once in a lifetime” are now happening every month. And while some people would rather stop talking about climate altogether, I refuse to. We only have one planet, and protecting it will take all of us rolling up our sleeves and standing together to defend our air, our water, our communities, and the places we call home. There is one thing that unites and undergirds everything this regime is doing, all the wars, and the destruction of our planet: Fossil fuels. Reading this message, you may wonder: What difference can one person really make? But here's what I've learned in my decades of activism: Individual actions, when multiplied across thousands of people, become a force that no one can ignore. That collective power is how change has always happened, and it’s why I want to share something concrete and actionable today. I love these 10 suggestions from the David Suzuki Foundation for what each of us can do to shrink our footprint and save our planet. For those who don’t recognize Suzuki’s name, he is a beloved Canadian scientist and environmentalist who has written more than 50 books and inspired generations to care for our planet. | 10 powerful ways each of us can reduce our environmental impact and drive climate progress: 1. Urge government to take bold, ambitious climate action now. 2. Use energy wisely — and save money too! 3. Get charged up with renewables. 4. Eat for a climate-stable planet. 5. Start a climate conversation. 6. Green your commute. 7. Consume less, waste less, enjoy life more. 8. Invest in renewables and divest from fossil fuels. 9. Mobilize for local climate action. 10. Get politically active and VOTE. So here's my ask: Take a moment to really consider these ten actions and pick three that you're ready to commit to. It could be something you're already doing that you want to do more intentionally, or it could be something completely new that challenges you to go further. Friends,
For the last 18 days, America has been at war with Iran.
The costs to our troops, to everyday Americans, and to innocent Iranian civilians — even schoolchildren — have already been devastating.
And the truth is simple: This war is deeply unpopular and illegal.
The Constitution makes plain that only Congress has the authority to declare war. Yet President Trump has escalated his use of our military to carry out hostilities all over the globe without Congress, while threatening military action against many more countries.
We’re at war because of the unilateral actions of one man — without the debate and vote the law requires. That’s exactly the kind of “kingly behavior” the founders of this country warned against.
We owe our service members better than this. They serve with such skill and bravery. But as our experiences in Vietnam and Iraq have shown, even the bravest patriotic service cannot overcome poor decision-making by our President, and a Congress unwilling to check this abuse of authority .
I introduced a bipartisan War Powers Resolution to end U.S. hostilities against Iran unless Congress explicitly authorizes them — and unfortunately, it failed because Senate Republicans blocked it from moving forward.
Americans do not want this war — and it’s critical that we speak out and make our voices heard. Call your members of Congress — especially if you’re represented by Republican representatives or senators — at (202) 224-3121 and demand they do their constitutional duty to hold this administration accountable.
Thank you for speaking out,
Tim Kaine

The question isn't whether God changed His mind about the Jews.

The question is whether He lied.

Rahab said in Joshua 2 that God gave Israel the land.

Scripture never says that promise was transferred to the Church. In fact, the New Testament says the exact opposite (Romans 11:25-29).

If God's promise to Israel can expire with time... then no promise of God is secure and He is a liar. Period.

God's character is tied to His promises. There's no third option. _

Remember, don't forget to think._
_Truth isn 't always easy. It challenges, it confronts, and sometimes...it costs. But I've made a decision...I will speak it anyway. Clearly. Boldly. Without compromise. body:
[1]Justice Democrats

Peter,

I have some disappointing news: Justice Democrats-endorsed Junaid Ahmed
narrowly lost his primary fight in Illinois’ 8th congressional district to
a corporate-backed opponent yesterday.

This was the first primary election where AIPAC, Crypto, and AI combined
forces to buy a seat in Congress, and unfortunately, they succeeded.

They flooded this district with over $6 million in the final month of the
race to prop up a right-wing politician, outspending Junaid by more than 5
to 1.

The winner, former corporate Congresswoman Melissa Bean, embodies the
exact type of establishment Democrat that voters are fed up with: another
corporate shill who will rubber-stamp Wall Street and Silicon Valley’s
billionaire agenda — which is exactly why these lobbies joined forces to
elect her.

Make no mistake: this loss is a blow to our democracy and a failure of the
Democratic establishment that has allowed lobbies like AIPAC, Crypto, and
AI to buy our elections.

Junaid is the type of leader Democratic voters are clamoring for — someone
unbought with the political courage to take on these corporate lobbies
head-on and deliver a bold, progressive vision that meets the demands of
working-class communities in IL and nationwide.

It took AIPAC, AI, and Crypto coming together to spend millions
whitewashing Bean’s right-wing record in Congress to elect her.

We may have lost this one, but the corporate establishment has to pull out
every stop to even have a chance of winning races this cycle — and that’s
a signal of our movement’s power.

Rumor has it Dan Meuser is quietly holding a **two-day fundraiser at Mar-a-Lago** this weekend, with a minimum entry fee of $3,500 a person.
Families here are dealing with rising health care, grocery, and gas prices and struggling to keep the lights on _because of our congressman 's votes._ And he's at a gold-plated beach resort down in Florida partying with the same ultra-wealthy donor class he sold us out to.

Farmers in Iowa especially are suffering the brunt of these effects. I've spoken to farmers and I hear the same thing over and over; the tariffs are shrinking key markets and squeezing family farms by making equipment, fertilizers, and diesel fuel much more expensive. This is a recipe for disaster.

Even though members of her own party are denouncing the tariffs, Mariannette Miller-Meeks refuses to grow a backbone and take a stand for her constituents. **If she won't do it, I will.**

I'm running for office because I'm more than ready to march into Congress and speak truth to power. Party politics and corporate interests don't scare me, Peter. If a policy is hurting the people of IA-01, trust that my voice will be the first to ring out in their defense. But I can't get there alone.

Growing up as a typical American Jew, I had it drilled into my head from a very young age that a strong Israel was a necessary condition for my safety. America was our home, sure, but as the grandson of a Holocaust survivor, I knew the history--at any moment our security could be shattered. Only the guaranteed protection of a Jewish state, made possible in part through the steadfast support of our Jewish community and all its institutions, could ensure my well-being in the long term.
It has been a long time since this claim made much sense to me. But in recent years it has become abundantly clear not only that this claim is false but that it is in fact the inverse of our current reality. Because here's the truth: There is nothing making Jews in America less safe today than the actions of Israel's far-right government--actions that too many of our mainstream Jewish institutions still refuse to disavow.
[Subscribed](https://substack.com/redirect/2/eyJlIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly9hYXJvbnJlZ3VuYmVyZy5zdWJzdGFjay5jb20vYWNjb3VudCIsInAiOjE5MTM2Nzg2MywicyI6NDk4MTE3MCwiZiI6dHJ1ZSwidSI6OTA1MDExOTIsImlhdCI6MTc3Mzg2NjE0OCwiZXhwIjoyMDg5NDQyMTQ4LCJpc3MiOiJwdWItMCIsInN1YiI6ImxpbmstcmVkaXJlY3QifQ.nVUVzNWFxKn-wpVAwmEQphz-EccT5KC4GwjtuDwyU48?)
Over the last few years, the Israeli government--through its hubris, brutality, and high-handed approach to American politics--has been doing everything in its power to turn the American public against it. Americans have watched the Israeli military commit an unending stream of [barbaric war crimes](https://substack.com/redirect/c468d438-1760-47f5-8fa4-5d1da21969d9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in Gaza, paid for in large part by our [tax dollars](https://substack.com/redirect/09f84191-e1e1-41b1-8b30-6006670bcd7f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). We've observed Israeli-backed settlers [commit](https://substack.com/redirect/d8fe7500-ab02-4113-a304-d88a32fbbaad?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) [lynchings](https://substack.com/redirect/0745e60f-8adf-4d7a-90e7-f69c41717ad2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and other apartheid-enforcing [mob violence](https://substack.com/redirect/0745e60f-8adf-4d7a-90e7-f69c41717ad2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in the West Bank, including against [American citizens](https://substack.com/redirect/0f79ddbe-7ef5-4c68-a666-20292ce5e49b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). We've seen the Israeli prime minister wield an [astonishing degree](https://substack.com/redirect/694737d6-3833-4437-968b-14216aa6f3ee?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) of influence over American politics and government policy. And most recently, we heard the Trump administration admit that it was pushed into launching its war against Iran because Israel wanted it to.
As Secretary of State Marco Rubio [explained](https://substack.com/redirect/74d4894a-6fb0-4005-abd3-462450aa7a39?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), the "imminent threat" to America that required such extraordinary military action was that "if Iran was attacked, and we believe that they would be attacked, that they would immediately come after us." Translation: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu was going to attack Iran, so President Trump had to jump on board--because apparently the alternatives, forcing the Israelis to back down or letting them act alone, were inconceivable.
This joint Israeli-American war is already deeply [unpopular](https://substack.com/redirect/94ae8973-a6e4-45ca-a0a6-c8aaa22636db?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). It will become more unpopular still as the costs (currently over a [billion dollars a day](https://substack.com/redirect/4c3425e7-652d-441e-a20d-2abd59a51530?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)) and the losses (at least 13 Americans have been killed) and the horrors (Iranians digging mass graves for the more than [150 elementary school girls](https://substack.com/redirect/961ee343-8b88-4956-9006-49b91eb1bd3d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) our government killed and [toxic black clouds](https://substack.com/redirect/51bd92cc-7c00-4cc1-ab96-1959f4c8f16c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) raining carcinogens on millions of civilians) continue to pile up. That's bad news for Israel's standing with the American public, among whom a serious backlash against Israel has already been [building](https://substack.com/redirect/a4b243ff-e820-4620-a534-8f678b0c27b6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
Now, in an ideal world, a backlash against Israel would be just that--nobody would conflate the Israeli government with the Jewish people as a whole. Americans who are rightly angry about what they've been seeing from Netanyahu's regime should say, "Israel's government killed tens of thousands of children in Gaza" or "Israel's government dragged us into a nightmare conflict with Iran" or "Israel's government murdered my family." In an ideal world, nobody would say, "The Jews did these things."
But we don't live in that ideal world. And that's in part because of the radically pro-Israel posture of the majority of mainstream Jewish institutions in our country.
These groups--of course the political organizations like the American Israel Public Affairs Committee and the Anti-Defamation League, but also local community institutions ([Jewish](https://substack.com/redirect/7b526707-45b9-4512-95cf-bbc02ff9d037?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) [federations](https://substack.com/redirect/9afa5f21-301e-40f8-b1dd-cd0a58533231?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), [professional groups](https://substack.com/redirect/8f5da30d-4275-4843-921e-f0bfb32211ff?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), [campus leaders](https://substack.com/redirect/23c1cda2-e61d-4b7a-9413-311bffb34ab8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), [media outlets](https://substack.com/redirect/452f1c37-1f4c-4eae-a535-7733eb1c128c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), and [more](https://substack.com/redirect/28fd53ff-333f-4412-a16d-b4376d132bbe?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg))--have spent the last three years aggressively declaring that criticism of Israel equates to antisemitism, that anti-Zionist Jews are not real Jews, and that the American Jewish community will stand with Israel no matter what crimes the state commits. In short, they have been insisting that "Israel" and "Jews" should be conflated--or in the [words](https://substack.com/redirect/33e041f5-ed2f-4e65-b6ad-8c60c4f1f726?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) of Jonathan Greenblatt, the ADL president, "You cannot take the Zion out of Jewish identity, you cannot take the Zionism out of Judaism."
Given that chorus from the very organizations and leaders who claim they represent the Jewish community, you don't have to be a Nazi to start ascribing the Israeli regime's horrifying conduct to all Jews. You just have to be a relatively low-information gentile who's not familiar with the point of view of the [growing majority](https://substack.com/redirect/da88ae61-e155-4b46-ad1c-575b9663b2b2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) of actual American Jews, who are increasingly critical of Israel but whose views are suppressed by our mainline institutions.
Of course--and I imagine some readers have already shouted this at their screens in frustration--antisemites will always find a justification to hate Jews. They did so before Israel existed, and they would continue to do so if there were no ethnonationalist Jewish state or if America's Jewish establishment did break with Israel's regime.
But this argument misunderstands the nature of the threat American Jews face today. Yes, there have always been, and likely will always be, virulent antisemites out there. But a world where this kind of resentment is relegated to a minor fringe is very different from one where these ideas have infiltrated a much broader population.
A decade ago, your average podcast-listening young man was not likely to think in terms of "the Jews are causing this or that harm." But after years of watching a live-streamed genocide be committed by the Jewish state and rarely hearing any condemnation by mainstream American Jewish institutions, that is changing. And it's easy to imagine the change accelerating as those same Jewish organizations [celebrate](https://substack.com/redirect/3bb52e72-1bb7-41b8-9995-adf38e9463d3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) a war that is despised by the American people.
This change matters greatly. It's the difference between antisemitic provocateur Nick Fuentes being some freak few people have heard of, and Fuentes having such a large and influential following that people like Vice President JD Vance [hesitate to exclude him](https://substack.com/redirect/6d6e3464-af69-4db9-8157-b23a33f2f9d0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) from GOP spaces. Fuentes has grown his base dramatically since Oct. 7, largely because of his shrewd weaving together of young people's legitimate outrage over the Israeli government's conduct with his own classically vile "Protocols of the Elders of Zion"-style antisemitism. (A similar story could be told about other hugely powerful figures on the antisemitic right, like Tucker Carlson.)
To point out how antisemitism has been spreading is not to justify or legitimate its spread. On the contrary, it is to affirm that this is a real problem, and taking a problem seriously requires understanding it.
And so it must be said that the move Fuentes and his ilk are making--unequivocally equating Israel and the Jews--is functionally the same move that Jewish organizations make when they declare that criticism of Israeli policy is antisemitism, a charge the ADL recently [leveled](https://substack.com/redirect/88e618d0-7257-4300-9922-3e4303722b56?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) at California Governor Gavin Newsom for his relatively anodyne [description](https://substack.com/redirect/bb0a7a2a-a554-4a95-9f4a-34baaabacfae?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) of Israel as "sort of an apartheid state." (To be clear, Israel is an apartheid state, definitionally--a Jewish baby born today in a West Bank community will have full rights in Israel, a vote in national elections, and access to civilian courts; a Palestinian baby born in that same community will have no democratic rights, tight restrictions on their movement, frequent harassment from settlers, and no access to justice beyond what Israel's unaccountable military courts mete out. That's apartheid.)
For years, these mainstream Jewish institutions have insisted they could have it both ways--declaring that being a Jew in good standing in our community requires undying support for the state of Israel while also maintaining that American Jews cannot be held responsible for Israel's actions. But here's the thing: You cannot claim that everyone who criticizes Israel for indiscriminately killing children is an antisemite--that is, someone who hates all Jews--without implying that indiscriminately killing children is somehow a project undertaken by all Jews rather than the project of a specific out-of-control far-right government and its supporters. And if you repeat that message often enough, well, some people are going to start believing it.
It is perfectly legitimate for a backlash against the Israeli regime to be building here in the United States. Americans are tired of seeing Israel manipulate our political system to ensure that our taxpayer dollars continue to subsidize Israeli aggression. And the fact that this observation seems to rhyme with a classic antisemitic trope of Jewish puppet masters controlling all world governments does not make it less true that Israel exerts enormous influence over US politics--though it does underline the degree to which Israeli policy fails to consider the safety and interests of American Jews. Given these empirical realities, Americans have to be ideologically committed to Israel to be satisfied with the current state of Israeli-American relations.
But if a significant proportion of the US population metabolizes their anger toward Israel into resentment against Jews as a whole--an outcome that the rhetoric of America First's Nick Fuentes and the ADL's Jonathan Greenblatt both seem to be inviting--that is a more dangerous state of affairs than Jews in this country have faced in generations, as we saw recently in Michigan, where a man [attacked](https://substack.com/redirect/15c37121-3ed7-4a0d-a27b-30fc52d7c852?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) a synagogue after an Israeli airstrike in Lebanon killed four members of his family. Certainly, it's a less safe world for my Jewish sons than the one I had the privilege of growing up in, in which yes, there were antisemites, but they had no real path to take their hate to scale. Today, such paths exist, and it's possible we're already quite far down them.
Of course, the security of American Jews should not be the primary focus of public discourse right now. Iranian schoolgirls have been mass-murdered, ancient cities are getting carpet-bombed, American service members are under attack, and millions of people across multiple Middle Eastern countries are facing the dislocations, uncertainties, and horrors of war. These imminent crises all matter more than my long-term concerns about the growth of antisemitism in our country.

Still, this point deserves attention. The logic of Zionism rests heavily on the claim that Jewish safety necessitates a Jewish state. It is largely this desire--to protect our people, whom history has proved need protection--that has led so many national and local Jewish institutions to continue backing the Israeli regime, through apartheid and genocide and more. But this approach is self-defeating. Tying the honor and reputation of our people to the rogue government of an ethnostate is not making us safer. On the contrary, it's making American Jews more vulnerable to the kind of antisemitic mass politics that we haven't had to worry about in this country for a long time. That's what my Jewish sons have to look forward to. And it's not going to change until our mainline Jewish institutions start owning up to the danger they've created for all of us and start demonstrating, through their words and deeds, that Israel does not, in fact, equal the Jews.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/83208b3d-c402-4a4e-80c3-843f0b461cc4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
This essay appeared in _[The Boston Globe](https://substack.com/redirect/f267d237-c74d-4cad-9d6b-e18c526ddb63?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)_ and will be in Sunday's print edition.
One last thing. I know there are people--including people I love very, very dearly--who will strongly disagree with parts or all of this essay. All I can say is that this conversation is important to me in large part because Judaism is important to me, and I don't think I personally would be living in accordance with my Jewish values (values I learned from some of you) if I didn't speak up.

| | Dear Peter,
---
What does it take to make our redwood forests more resilient to wildfire? This is something I spend a lot of time thinking about as our land stewardship manager. The truth is, there is no single answer: we need time for forests to grow stronger, innovative approaches to ecological restoration, and the wisdom of long‐standing Indigenous practices. **With**** ****a****ll the t****ime ****I****’****ve**** ****spent**** in the forests**** of Harold Richardson Redwoods Reserve, ****I****’****ve**** seen ****the incredible**** things ****that ****happen when you combine ****all three.**

| | [Harold Richardson Redwoods Reserve](https://click.everyaction.com/k/127591827/608576638/-479769549?sourceid=1168358&ms=EM7&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9TVFJXTC9TVFJXTC8xLzg5NTc0IiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogIjBhMTczMWQxLTA5MjMtZjExMS05YTQ4LTAwMGQzYTE0YjY0MCIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=466D5XNhjImkS-pSOYPg775siFxBmZTt43UOo_EJdzo=&emci=041141cd-0322-f111-9a48-000d3a14b640&emdi=0a1731d1-0923-f111-9a48-000d3a14b640&ceid=1504551) is home to ancient giants, including one that is over 1,640 years old. The reserve is one of the planet’s most pristine redwood landscapes. These coast redwoods are tough and fire adapted. But as climate change supercharges wildfires, we must think differently about how to make these forests more resilient.

clean_body: What is the recipe for resilience?| | | | | Dear Peter, What does it take to make our redwood forests more resilient to wildfire? This is something I spend a lot of time thinking about as our land stewardship manager. The truth is, there is no single answer: we need time for forests to grow stronger, innovative approaches to ecological restoration, and the wisdom of long‐standing Indigenous practices. With all the time I’ve spent in the forests of Harold Richardson Redwoods Reserve, I’ve seen the incredible things that happen when you combine all three. | | | | is home to ancient giants, including one that is over 1,640 years old. The reserve is one of the planet’s most pristine redwood landscapes. These coast redwoods are tough and fire adapted. But as climate change supercharges wildfires, we must think differently about how to make these forests more resilient. | | | | In this case, thinking ‘differently’ means listening to the land. Harold Richardson Redwoods Reserve is in the ancestral lands of the Kashia Band of Pomo Indians, whose stewardship stretches back since time immemorial. In 2024, Save the Redwoods partnered with the Kashia to conduct the first prescribed burn on the property. Observing, adapting, and responding to what the forests need helps return ecological balance and natural resilience. | | | | Prescribed burning practices have been used for thousands of years to promote healthy habitats and prevent wildfires. By clearing the dense underbrush of the forest, we are removing flammable plant matter that can serve as fuel for megafires. The carefully planned burn restores natural fire resilience to the forest, returns nutrients to the soil, improves habitats for native species, and more. | | | | Now, we have a chance to shape an even more promising future for this land. If we can acquire 200 acres of land adjacent to the reserve, it will provide a vital buffer against threats like wildfires and climate change. . . Thank you for being part of this next chapter of the extraordinary Harold Richardson Redwoods Reserve. | | | Sincerely, Anthony Castaños Senior Land Stewardship Manager | | Photos by Coldwater Collective | | Help restore and protect the redwoods | | Save the Redwoods League220 Montgomery St, Suite 350San Francisco, CA 94104United States CONNECT WITH US | | | | | | ---|---|---|---|---|--- |

subject: We can change the page.

body:
We have to have a politics of integrity, not a politics of cowardice anymore
#
For so long, we have had political leadership — including in the Democratic Party — that has just wanted to play it safe.
That has just wanted to be neutral. Where so many people are motivated by their own individual political careers.
We have to have a politics of _integrity_ , not a politics of cowardice anymore.
We have to stand up for what is right in this country. **We can change the page**.
We will never get past Donald Trump if we continue to elect the same people and make the same decisions that got us here in the first place.
It does not matter your positions, your content, your ideas, how experienced you are. It doesn’t matter how much you work with them — they will choose their old friends _every single time_.
**Our future will not be different until we make a different choice.**
Together, we’ve built a movement fighting for critical issues, from Medicare for All to democratizing fundraising power in politics.
And to keep pushing forward, we must support progressives up and down the ballot who are facing off against opponents — from both parties — who are handing the keys to our country over to billionaires and special interests.
[Will you split a $5 contribution today between our movement and Courage to Change, our leadership PAC which supports grassroots candidates, so we can fight on behalf of working-class brawlers across the country who are running to make real change?](https://act.ocasiocortez.com/go/14659?c0=aoc-email-20260318-ctc.v4ohOh&refcode=em20260318-10995-P_FND_EGR_CTC&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=1&akid=10995%2E2526796%2EOO-ypU)

Alexandria

subject: We will take on President Trump. But we can’t do it alone.
body:

I want to be honest with you about something that would have sounded unthinkable just a few years ago.
Across the country, secretaries of state are quietly meeting to plan how to respond if Donald Trump tries to interfere with the 2026 elections.
We’re running tabletop exercises, coordinating with attorneys general, and preparing legal strategies in case the federal government attempts to meddle with voting, ballots, or certification.
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/read-em-24?refcode=260318em [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/read-em-24?refcode=260318em]
FIGHT BACK [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/read-em-24?refcode=260318em]
Think about that for a moment: State election officials in the United States of America are now planning for the possibility that the President and his allies might try to use federal power to disrupt elections.
That is not normal. But pretending the threat doesn’t exist would be irresponsible.
President Trump has already called for the federal government to “take over” elections. His Justice Department is suing states for access to sensitive voter data. Federal agents have seized ballots in Georgia and issued subpoenas in Arizona
And we are preparing for the same to happen here in Oregon. I’ve already started meeting with county clerks here in Oregon to make sure we are ready for anything President Trump tries to do to disrupt our elections.
As Oregon’s Secretary of State, my job is to protect our elections and defend the Constitution. That means making sure Oregon is ready for anything — intimidation at polling places, federal interference, attempts to disrupt mail voting, or efforts to block certification.
Democracy only survives if people defend it. And defending Oregon’s elections requires a strong grassroots team supporting our important work at this pivotal moment.
If you believe states — not presidents — should run elections, I’m asking you to step up today. Please contribute now to help us defend Oregon’s elections and ensure our democracy remains free, fair, and secure. >> [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/read-em-24?refcode=260318em]
DONATE NOW [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/read-em-24?refcode=260318em]
Thank you,

| | **Merced County Republican Party Endorses Alexandra Duarte for State Senate **

| MERCED COUNTY, CA — Alexandra Duarte, Republican candidate for California State Senate, today announced the endorsement of the Merced County Republican Party, a significant show of support from one of the region’s key Republican organizations. The endorsement continues the flood of endorsements, funding, and grassroots support building behind Duarte. For beleaguered liberal incumbent Marie Alvarado-Gil, it is yet another sign that conservative voters are rejecting her leftist record. For Duarte, the support from Merced County Republicans reinforces the campaign’s effort to build a broad base of backing rooted in local communities, neighborhood concerns, and frustration with the direction of state government. “Merced County families want conservative representation they can trust and be proud of,” said Alexandra Duarte. “I’m grateful to have the support of the Merced County Republican Party and proud to have them with us in our fight to take back Senate District 4.” ###

body:
Leaders We Deserve candidates Demi Palecek and Nabeela Syed won their primaries last night — without taking a dime of corporate cash.
# [](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/852?refcode=em20260318-1-b&t=1&akid=3261%2E587540%2EIY7cuB)
Peter,
**Last night, two Leaders We Deserve candidates won their primaries in Illinois!**
That makes five victories for us so far in the 2026 cycle, and every one of those candidates ran to challenge the status quo. Last night was further proof that our movement is working.
**In Illinois House District 13, Demi Palecek won the Democratic primary in Chicago’s North Side.** In a five-way race, she took on candidates bankrolled by the same corporate powerful special interests and super PAC money that has had a stranglehold on Illinois politics for decades.
Demi was outspent 6:1 by one of her opponents who was backed with hundreds of thousands of dollars from DraftKings-funded super PAC “American Future,” Mark Zuckerberg’s super PAC, “Making Our Tomorrow,” and other dark money groups determined to protect their corporate interests. **They thought they could buy this seat — _they were wrong._**
We were proud to play a major role in supporting her candidacy, investing over $110,000 in her campaign, conducting polling in the race, knocking doors in the district, and sharing Demi’s message online. Last night showed that Democrats don’t need to sell out to win — there is a path to victory for young candidates who are strategic with their money, know how to organize in their community, and have a clear vision voters actually want to support. Demi stuck to her values, out maneuvered the special interests, _and won._
Demi has spent years showing up for her community. Organizing women’s marches, sheltering people seeking abortion care, and running monthly mutual aid events that have served over 4,000 meals. She’s stood on the frontlines for families that have been wrongfully detained by ICE, including her own. When she gets to the state legislature, she’ll show what it’s like to lead with integrity and be the working class fighter her district deserves.
**In Illinois State Senate District 26, Nabeela Syed advanced in her primary and will face off with Republican incumbent Darby Hills in November.** She has a real opportunity to flip the district and prove that when we back young, bold progressive fighters, we can compete _anywhere._
Since flipping a Republican state house district in 2022, Nabeela hasn't stopped fighting for working people. She’s passed legislation to penalize pharmaceutical corporations that hike up drug prices, protect sexual assault survivors from having their DNA used against them, and close a loophole cutting low income families off from heating assistance. That’s what delivering real results for your constituents looks like.
**Demi and Nabeela won their primaries, but their fight isn’t over.** Corporate PACs and dark money groups will continue pouring money into Demi’s race to take her down, and flipping Nabeela’s district won’t be easy.
Leaders We Deserve doesn’t take _any_ special interest money or corporate cash, and neither do our candidates. That means they rely on grassroots supporters like you, Peter, to keep them in this fight.
**[Will you pitch in $5 to help us make sure Demi and Nabeela have the resources they need to win? The work that wins in November starts right now.](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20260318_1_results.CgPydq&refcode=em20260318-3261-b&amount=5&t=2&akid=3261%2E587540%2EIY7cuB)**

This is what a winning movement looks like. Let’s keep going.
Thank you,
David Hogg

| | [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/127593130/608581456/-1456264782?refcode=KH_ATA_EM_FR_SaveAct_260318_T1_1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNjEvMS8xMTA5NjQiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiN2E1MTBiMzYtMGUyMy1mMTExLTlhNDgtMDAwZDNhMTRiNjQwIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=NgWUHkVfOZP3gNI97otg11bqmcvgDheUrA0A3Py-K9g=) Team, right now, there's a bill gaining traction in Washington that should concern us all. It's called the SAVE Act.

**Here's what you need to know:** this bill would require every American to present expensive, difficult-to-obtain government documents, such as a passport or certified birth certificate, before they can even register to vote in federal elections.

But [_over 21 million voting-age citizens_](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/127593131/608581457/2004686021?refcode=KH_ATA_EM_FR_SaveAct_260318_T1_1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNjEvMS8xMTA5NjQiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiN2E1MTBiMzYtMGUyMy1mMTExLTlhNDgtMDAwZDNhMTRiNjQwIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=NgWUHkVfOZP3gNI97otg11bqmcvgDheUrA0A3Py-K9g=&emci=56292198-0423-f111-9a48-000d3a14b640&emdi=7a510b36-0e23-f111-9a48-000d3a14b640&ceid=28432238) don't have a proof-of-citizenship document – like a birth certificate, passport or naturalization certificate – or don't have easy access to one. People of color are more likely not to have a document proving citizenship, and married women will also face voting difficulties due to name mismatches.

That means **millions** of eligible voters could be blocked from registering this year and from ever casting a ballot, which is _exactly_ what our opponents want.

[**_If you’re ready to push back on efforts to restrict the vote, we need you in this fight with us. Can you support our campaign by chipping in $5 or anything you can afford right now?_**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/127593132/608581458/-1456264782?refcode=KH_ATA_EM_FR_SaveAct_260318_T1_1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNjEvMS8xMTA5NjQiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiN2E1MTBiMzYtMGUyMy1mMTExLTlhNDgtMDAwZDNhMTRiNjQwIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=NgWUHkVfOZP3gNI97otg11bqmcvgDheUrA0A3Py-K9g=)

This terrible bill was introduced by Chip Roy, the current representative for TX-21 and my 2024 opponent. And make no mistake, Trump's handpicked candidate for this open seat is fully behind it and will help advance policies like the SAVE Act in Congress to disenfranchise voters.

**When I get to Congress, I will oppose every effort to restrict ballot access. Full stop.**

That means defending mail and online registration, opposing laws like the SAVE Act, and making sure every eligible Texan can cast their ballot without jumping through hoops.

Because this isn’t just about one bill.

The right to vote is the foundation for everything working families are fighting for. Affordability. Healthcare. Equal pay. None of it is possible if people are pushed out of the political process before they ever get a say.

[**_If you want to stop the SAVE Act and protect the right to vote, the most important thing you can do right now is help us win this seat. And I’ve done it all while balancing the budget and passing the largest property tax cut in county history.

As Governor, I’ll bring my affordability agenda statewide, investing in:

* Jobs and wages that build future
* Affordable, safe housing across Wisconsin
* Health care that reaches people
* Climate action that creates jobs
* Strong schools and early learning

On the other hand, Tom Tiffany has made it clear that he opposes common-sense reforms to make life more affordable, voting down proposals to provide child care, tax relief, and infant formula funds to working Wisconsinites.

I've seen it before.

_And I stopped it before._

**It started in 1998 when I was Speaker of the House.**

The Clinton Administration attempted to fundamentally corrupt the U.S. Census.

Their plan was called _" statistical sampling."_

**In plain English, it would have allowed unelected bureaucrats to manufacture population numbers instead of counting _real people, one at a time._**

Red states would be undercounted.
Blue states would be completely inflated.
Congressional seats would be rigged before a single vote was cast.

It was a direct assault on representative government, Peter.

_**So I sued Bill Clinton --and won.**_

The Supreme Court sided with me in a nail-biting 5-4 ruling.
They agreed the only legitimate way to count the Census was by a _strict, physical headcount._

name: Ruben Gallego
subject: I’m a no on Markwayne Mullin
disclaimer_text: Paid For By Gallego for Arizona
body:
Even if he does get confirmed as Secretary of Homeland Security, he won’t be running it. That creep Stephen Miller will be the one in charge, and Mullin is going to follow his orders.
#

Peter, it's Ruben.
I actually get along with Markwayne Mullin. We don’t agree on much, but we’ve worked together in the past when we were in alignment. I’m from Arizona, and I won’t ever rule out working across the aisle with someone.
But that said, there’s no chance I can support him for Secretary of Homeland Security. None.
He’d be in charge of Homeland Security Investigations. The people working there are tasked with some of the most serious responsibilities — human trafficking, the exploitation of children, cybercrime, drug smuggling. They’re meant to target terrorists and cartels.
HSI has been taken off that work and redirected to mass deportations for the past year. And as of about a month ago, they’ve been directed to investigate the 2020 election in Arizona.
I asked Mullin about that today. Point blank, I asked him if Biden won in 2020. Put aside the fact that multiple independent audits and 14 court cases found that to be the case, or that he didn’t want to upset Trump.
Why — after everything that’s already happened — should HSI be taken off the human trafficking, child exploitation, and narcotics beats to investigate a free and fair election that happened six years ago?
He didn’t have an answer, and that’s not surprising. Because even if he does get confirmed as Secretary of Homeland Security, he won’t be running it. That creep Stephen Miller will be the one in charge, and Mullin is going to follow his orders.
I’m not voting for him. I don’t think anyone should. And if you agree, please:
[**Add your name and sign on in opposition to Markwayne Mullin’s nomination as Secretary of Homeland Security.**](https://act.gallegoforarizona.com/signup/260318-MWM-EM/?refcode=em260318-1-120&akid=4091%2E734936%2E9L0KaE)
[SIGN ON](https://act.gallegoforarizona.com/signup/260318-MWM-EM/?source=em260318-1-120&akid=4091%2E734936%2E9L0KaE)
Thanks,
Ruben

clean_body: This special election on April 21 is essential to countering the GOP power grab. | Peter, here’s the latest on the fight for fair maps in Virginia. Last year, President Trump and his MAGA allies forced unprecedented, mid-decade redraws in Texas, North Carolina, and Missouri. It’s all part of their scheme to gain an unfair advantage in the midterms this fall. But some states are fighting back to level the playing field. Our eyes are on Virginia, where state leaders have proposed a temporary measure to counter these egregious Republican gerrymanders. Unlike lawmakers in those Republican-controlled states, who manipulated their maps without the consent of their constituents, leaders in Virginia have put the question to the people in a special election on April 21. Early voting is underway right now — and the NDRC is on the ground to help voters send a resounding message that they reject this GOP power grab. = Our work is essential as Trump and his allies put more pressure on state lawmakers to manipulate maps ahead of the midterms. Right now, Governor DeSantis and lawmakers in Florida are planning a special legislative session in the spring to make their already gerrymandered map even more extreme. Peter, it’s JB Pritzker.
I’ll get right to it: Jon Ossoff is Donald Trump and MAGA’s top target for defeat in the midterm elections, and he needs your support today to defend his battleground seat. [**Will you join me in supporting Jon by chipping in to his reelection campaign ahead of his first end-of-quarter deadline of 2026?**](https://act.electjon.com/go/32?c0=ossoff-em-mar26.B6mAX1&refcode=em260318-2-subs&t=2&akid=1883%2E5691347%2EGWy8sr)
**Every right and freedom we hold dear is on the line in November.**
Voting rights. Our democracy. The rule of law. The safety and security of Americans across the nation.
Our ability to defend these longstanding pillars of our democracy hinges on the midterm elections and whether Democrats can take back power from the tyrant in the White House.
Jon’s Senate race in Georgia will be the most critical election this year in fighting back against the onslaught of attacks from Donald Trump.
But Republicans are already pulling every dirty trick in the book to defeat him.
The GOP and their far-right Super PACs have already spent over $10 million in Georgia to tip the scales in their favor. And last month, Donald Trump visited Georgia, where he personally attacked Jon and continued to spew his Big Lie conspiracies on stage in front of hundreds of MAGA supporters.
It’s clear Republicans are all in to flip this seat red and lock in their majority for the long run.
We can’t let that happen — not when the stakes are this high.
I know Jon can win big in November. After all, this is the very seat that secured the Democratic majority in 2021. But it’s going to take all of us to emerge victorious. That’s why I’m asking:
[**Peter, will you join me in supporting Jon Ossoff by making a donation to his reelection campaign today? He is facing his most important fundraising deadline yet at the end of this month and needs your support to crush his goal.**](https://act.electjon.com/go/32?c0=ossoff-em-mar26.B6mAX1&refcode=em260318-2-subs&t=3&akid=1883%2E5691347%2EGWy8sr)

Thanks for standing with Jon and me.
– JB Pritzker

name: Gina Hinojosa
subject: Texas Latinos turned out in huge numbers
body:
Greg Abbott and his billionaire friends are going to spend anything to get the Latino vote.
# [](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)[](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)
Latinos were the real drivers in the primary election, Peter.
And people are starting to take notice. Take a look at these headlines:
[](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/625?c0=em_ms_gh_20260318_1_latinovote.5k4Bwq&refcode=em20260318-776&amount=5&t=1&akid=776%2E299639%2EkPUOuE)
[](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/625?c0=em_ms_gh_20260318_1_latinovote.5k4Bwq&refcode=em20260318-776&amount=5&t=2&akid=776%2E299639%2EkPUOuE)_Via AP and POLITICO_
Texas Democrats turned out in higher numbers than Republicans. And in majority-Latino counties, turnout surged compared to the last midterm primary. With Latino Texans making up 25% of the state’s electorate, that kind of turnout can shape statewide outcomes — _especially this November._
I’m especially proud of the Rio Grande Valley, the border region where I was born and raised, and where the vast majority of residents are Latino. In a place that’s been overlooked for too long and has seen huge political shifts in recent years, people showed up and made their voices heard loud and clear.
We have a real opportunity to build on the energy we just saw. If we focus on voter contact, share my message, and keep people engaged, we have a real chance of beating Greg Abbott.
**We have already seen how the Latino vote can shift outcomes in Texas. We saw it in Taylor Rehmet’s race, we saw it in Leander and Robstown, and we’re going to see it happen again in November.**
There is no doubt that Abbott and his billionaire buddies will spend the next few months competing hard for Latino voters, so we’re going to need all of the grassroots support and resources to counter their efforts.
**[So I’m asking, if you are able to help build on this momentum and power my work through November, will you chip in $5 today?](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/625?c0=em_ms_gh_20260318_1_latinovote.5k4Bwq&refcode=em20260318-776&amount=5&t=3&akid=776%2E299639%2EkPUOuE)**
[Donate $5 »](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/625?c0=em_ms_gh_20260318_1_latinovote.5k4Bwq&amount=5&refcode=em20260318-776&t=22&akid=776%2E299639%2EkPUOuE)
Thank you for your support,
— Gina Hinojosa

Dear friend,
My name is Alex Kelloff , and I’m running for Congress in Colorado’s 3rd District. I’m a fourth-generation Coloradan whose family roots in this district go back to 1893. I’m running to lower the cost of living, safeguard healthcare, protect our public lands and water, safeguard our democracy, and stop us from going to unnecessary wars of choice.
WE ARE IN A STRONG POSITION TO FLIP CO-03 FROM JEFF HURD AND THE REPUBLICANS ON NOVEMBER 3RD.
For over 10 months, our campaign has been doing exactly what campaigns should do - putting in the work. We didn’t wait until the last minute to jump into this race. Instead, we’ve spent our time traveling the district, listening to voters, and building support one person and one community at a time.
Our hard work has paid off:
* Over $1 million raised
* Top 4% of all new Democratic congressional challengers nationwide in fundraising
* 2,400+ individual donors and growing
* Received more than 2.5x the assembly delegates of our opponent in the three most populous counties in CD-3 - Pueblo, Mesa, and La Plata
And that’s what happens when you:
* Visit all 27 counties in Colorado’s 3rd District
* Drive thousands of miles through all four seasons
* Hold more than 120 events with voters across the district
* Earn the endorsement of previous CD3 representative and former candidates for the seat: John Salazar, Sol Sandoval, Gail Schwartz and Diane Mitsch Bush
We are building a broad coalition across the district and continuing to gain momentum every day.
We invite you to join our team as we continue the work needed to flip this seat blue in the midterms. [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/2603-q1-ak]
Best,
Alex Kelloff

Hi friend,

As a mom, I know how hard it is to raise kids today.

It’s made even harder by rising prices and impossible choices — many have to decide between groceries and medicine. I see how hard-working families are still struggling as costs keep climbing.

It shouldn’t take men and women working multiple jobs to take care of their families. That’s not what this country is about.

I’m running for Congress to fight for working families — to make sure they get the support they need and to ensure we are doing everything possible to help families not just get by, but truly thrive.

I want to take this fight to Washington because our communities deserve someone who understands the experience and who will fight to deliver the kind of relief families need. | | | **[Trump is an imminent danger to us all, and he needs to be removed by impeachment, 25th Amendment, or whatever legal means is available.](https://default.salsalabs.org/Teb50bcdf-6ff4-4bd6-b37e-d5ba24416682/368d17ff-e836-4168-8049-c5f0900fbbf9)** **Republicans, this means you too. You need to stop hiding on the sidelines, and work with Democrats to make this happen.** Trump has plunged us into a completely unnecessary war, he appears ready to use any weapon, and he has picked fights with just about every nation on Earth. So when he tells wildly obvious lies about how the war is going, or tells us about conversations with imaginary presidents, or shows a myriad of other signs of cognitive decline, it’s a big, damn, deal. Republicans -- you put this monster in power, even when it was abundantly clear how dangerous it would be. And now he’s got his unsteady finger on the button, and America faces an existential threat. It doesn’t matter if it may hurt you in a Republican primary, or get you nasty letters, or worse--you are elected leaders, your nation is in danger, and you need to lead NOW. **[Sign on: “Trump is Dangerously Unhinged and Needs to Be Removed NOW”](https://default.salsalabs.org/Tec74c94d-5881-42ee-bad6-847280c0d015/368d17ff-e836-4168-8049-c5f0900fbbf9)**

name: Combat Veteran John James
subject: Our military deserves better
disclaimer_text: Paid for by John James for MI, 35744 Van Dyke Avenue, Sterling Heights, MI 48312
body:
| | | Patriot, As a combat veteran, I am deeply disturbed by the way some in the media are treating the men and women of our military. I proudly served our country as an Army aviation officer, flying Apache helicopters and logging more than 750 combat hours during Operation Iraqi Freedom. My time in uniform taught me the meaning of duty, discipline, and what it truly means to put others before yourself. That’s why it’s so frustrating to see politicians, pundits, and members of the mainstream media throwing our military under the bus. **As a veteran, I will always stand with our troops. That will never change.** Today, I just want to ask you something simple. [**Will you personally let me know that you stand with our military, too?**](http://links.jjformichigan.com/u/click?_t=70fde66bc0554ca7a14c16f5ebafdbd9&_m=6e22c0c6dc0b4447ba53c1a92bb87da7&_e=Iwt94RkMKe853E0ZSSrHnD_J6XIlPHjK1FivNN3bXoiLWVnGGeimn-payxHwPglSQ35Zo03p7NRc8d7jkL73mCZEvjAtPKV1m_X5jc77Q5x-Qlfn48lxHwTvIzxpcBcMTteB8T46WR-uosZZXFO5TBmpxGHh6Rlf1f2LvdvB9JVmy_uze40En4PJLc8LuIZeGn8bNsWaKTCvN5zn3TkCVZs9GTGEj5eCtCGdj-hbIBwlhEi78cH-cHIcawD-KP49npE61uEGPiv2_iMY6QVU9uHIV_ZZW-5EAYNlGoTMc-Gt69c_LIXJ4cHQ4X5tScJcDnklcr24klhtH-QK4rBkGMYi_P2SRcXcAdxQJ1URKOeQl77rbgiY_EtqPQlqRwNDxn57L6qkuoKG9EqNdbMZuGuGo40HKAOkzR3AXxcQVmjNAzRSz1Dp36Sqq063YF69)

| | **I’m proud to share that I’ve been endorsed by Reproductive Justice Maryland. ** Their mission is a vital one: championing reproductive justice as a fundamental human right for every Marylander. Like them, I believe that everyone deserves the freedom to make informed decisions about their bodies, their health, and their futures—free from discrimination or government interference. [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/127595776/608590035/-1274932420?refcode=E28833-20260318-ReproductiveJustice-Image-AbortionReproRightsA&amount=15&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTIvMS85MTI0OSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI3NTk3NGY2OS0xNjIzLWYxMTEtOWE0OC0wMDBkM2ExNGI2NDAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=MvFi3riOS_TwYTmL3xd7Vq0BaUFocAb2-EDcjlQ24z8=) As one of the youngest women serving in Congress—and the youngest in the Maryland delegation—these issues aren’t abstract to me. Wade_ and ensure every Marylander has the freedom they deserve. **[But I can’t take on this fight alone. Their mission is a vital one: championing reproductive justice as a fundamental human right for every Marylander. Like them, I believe that everyone deserves the freedom to make informed decisions about their bodies, their health, and their futures—free from discrimination or government interference. = As one of the youngest women serving in Congress—and the youngest in the Maryland delegation—these issues aren’t abstract to me. We have seen the devastating consequences of extreme laws that strip autonomy, delay lifesaving care, and disrupt the ability to plan one’s own family. I believe that decisions about our bodies belong to us, not politicians or judges. That’s why I’m fighting to codify the protections once afforded by Roe v. Wade and ensure every Marylander has the freedom they deserve. = | = I came to Congress to ensure our rights aren’t left up to partisan theater and extreme politicians. It’s not enough to talk about what’s at stake; we must act. Onward, Sarah Elfreth | * = | | | ---|---|---|--- Congresswoman Sarah Elfreth broke barriers in 2024, becoming the youngest woman ever elected to Congress from Maryland. She went to Congress with one thing in mind: delivering for Maryland families on the issues that matter most. Whether it's standing up for federal workers, supporting veterans, protecting the Chesapeake Bay, or tackling the affordability crisis head-on, Sarah is on the front lines, fighting for what is right. And Sarah has delivered on her promises. She has spent her first year in the House advocating for the Third District, successfully passing five bills into law, solving over 1,000 constituent cases, and bringing tens of millions in funding back to her community. She learned her work ethic and tenacity from growing up in a union household and honed her skills of problem-solving and collaborating over six years in the Maryland State Senate. name: LeftNet
subject: [Contact your representative] Demand Congress put a stop to Trump’s illegal war in Iran.
body:
If Congress does not act now, Trump will keep doing whatever he wants with our troops and taxpayer money.
#
Last month, Donald Trump dropped a bomb in Iran that killed 175 people — most of them being children — with no congressional approval and no clear imminent threat.
Let’s be clear on what this is. This is an illegal and unconstitutional act of war.
Trump campaigned on a promise to be the “President of peace”, but instead, he’s escalating yet _another_ forever war, putting American service members in harm’s way, risking innocent lives, and treating the Constitution like it is optional.
We’ve seen this happen before. When presidents claim they are acting to “protect democracy” or “uphold the people’s will,” the biggest winners are never the people they claim to be fighting for — **it’s the corporations and contractors that profit from instability, weapons, and oil.**
Even Trump’s own intelligence officials have said Iran was not close to developing a nuclear weapon. And now, Trump has made it clear this is about regime change.
That is exactly how the country was dragged into the Iraq war, and we can’t let it happen again.
This war is not ours to fight. And if Congress does not act now, Trump will keep doing whatever he wants with our troops and taxpayer money. **[If you agree, contact your representative today and demand Congress put a stop to Trump’s illegal war.](https://act.leftnet.org/go/22439?source=em20260318-1528&t=1&akid=1528%2E2118727%2EO3sdF1)**
**[CONTACT YOUR REPRESENTATIVE ››](https://act.leftnet.org/go/22439?source=em20260318-1528&t=2&akid=1528%2E2118727%2EO3sdF1)**

Thank you,
— LeftNet

Dear Friend, Never in a million years did I think I would be writing an email like this. **[But the truth is, my family and I are out of options. And you’re our only hope.](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.) **
---
| | This is a photo of my brother, Anthony DeLustro. Anthony spent more than 20 years serving citizens as an NYPD cop, hunting down dangerous drug dealers and busting up drug dens. On 9/11, he helped evacuate hundreds of people from one of the buildings just before it collapsed. Since that day, he’s been battling cancer and Ground Zero Lung from the toxic fumes. We really thought Anthony had been through the worst of it. And when he told us he was taking a police job in a small South Carolina town so he could spend his golden years close to his grandkids, I was so relieved.
---
| [](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)
---
| | How could I have known he was about to face the greatest danger of his life? I’m not talking about a drug dealer or a terrorist or even cancer... **...but a local prosecutor hellbent on destroying my brother for defending himself when he was the victim of a road rage incident.** Let me explain. The day Anthony was attacked, he was off duty. He and his wife had stopped for lunch after spending the morning at a “Coffee With A Cop” community event. And as they tried to pull out of the crowded restaurant parking lot... ...another driver, in a fit of road rage, jumped out of his car and began screaming threats at my brother. Anthony tried to calm him down. But the man attacked him, striking him over and over. My brother could see the situation was spiraling out of control. He pulled out his badge and told the man he was under arrest. But instead of complying... ...the man knocked the badge out of Anthony’s hand. Then he got in his car and tried to flee, dragging my brother with his vehicle and running over his legs. In that moment, Anthony knew he was about to be crushed to death in front of his own wife. So he fired a single shot into his attacker’s arm, bringing the car to a stop. Anthony’s quick thinking saved his life. But the road rage driver who attacked him died at the scene. When I got the call that Anthony had been assaulted and was in the hospital with serious injuries, I couldn’t believe what had happened. I was so relieved he was alive. **But my relief turned into shock when my brother was arrested and charged with murder.** He hadn’t even recovered from his injuries when the local prosecutor dragged him in front of a judge and had him locked up in jail. He’s already spent 10 months behind bars. And he’s facing up to **30** **years** in prison. My Friend, Anthony is 64 years old. If he’s convicted... **...he’ll likely spend the rest of his life locked up -- and die in prison -- for defending himself.** **[That’s why I’m writing you -- someone I’ve never met -- to ask you to help my brother.](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)**
---
| | Because what they’re doing to Anthony is an outrage. I might not be a cop... But to me, if a police officer puts you under arrest, you don’t resist. And you certainly don’t physically attack the officer, then try to flee the scene. My brother may have been off duty. But you know that as an off-duty officer, he had the authority -- and even the responsibility -- to make an arrest to protect the public. What does this prosecutor expect off-duty officers to do -- just let angry, violent offenders beat them up, resist arrest, and then walk away like nothing happened?
---
| [](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)
---
| | My Friend, Anthony doesn’t deserve this. He’s a good man who’s well-respected by his fellow officers. He served as a cop for four decades and never once faced discipline. He has a spotless record full of awards and commendations. So to watch my brother’s life be torn apart like this is just heartbreaking. It’s been hard on his family too. Several years ago, Anthony and his wife took their two granddaughters into their home. They’ve been raising them ever since. In some races — especially state and local ones — the share is even higher.** A tiny handful of ultra-wealthy individuals now have the financial power to shape huge portions of our political system. And too often, the policies that follow serve those same billionaires — not working families trying to afford housing, health care, and groceries. **Under Trump, we're seeing the consequences of this billionaires-win agenda: tax breaks for the wealthy, corporate loopholes left wide open, and powerful interests pushing policies that make Americans sicker and poorer.** _That's not the democracy our founders envisioned._ I believe our government should work for people, not the powerful who can write the biggest checks. That's why I've fought for stronger campaign finance rules, transparency in political spending, and policies that level the playing field. But until those reforms pass, one of the most powerful ways to fight back is through grassroots support. Small donations from people like you are how we counterbalance billionaire money and prove that a campaign powered by ordinary Americans can still compete.
