clean_body: | | | | The scale of billionaire money flooding into our elections has reached a staggering level. A recent analysis found that 300 billionaire families accounted for nearly 19% of all federal campaign contributions in 2024. In some races — especially state and local ones — the share is even higher. A tiny handful of ultra-wealthy individuals now have the financial power to shape huge portions of our political system. And too often, the policies that follow serve those same billionaires — not working families trying to afford housing, health care, and groceries. Under Trump, we're seeing the consequences of this billionaires-win agenda: tax breaks for the wealthy, corporate loopholes left wide open, and powerful interests pushing policies that make Americans sicker and poorer. That's not the democracy our founders envisioned. I believe our government should work for people, not the powerful who can write the biggest checks. That's why I've fought for stronger campaign finance rules, transparency in political spending, and policies that level the playing field. But until those reforms pass, one of the most powerful ways to fight back is through grassroots support. Donald Trump just made it clear: he believes he has “the absolute right”
to ignore the Supreme Court.^1

After the Court ruled that many of the tariffs he imposed last year were
illegal, Trump didn’t take responsibility. He didn’t respect the ruling.
Instead, he lashed out, attacked the justices, and is now threatening to
impose a new wave of tariffs anyway.

This is what happens when one man believes he is above the law: he tries
to bend the courts to his will, exploit loopholes, and bully the system
whenever it doesn’t give him what he wants.

He has repeatedly ignored court orders, abused the Shadow Docket, and now
he’s escalating — putting our economy, our trade relationships, and our
democracy at risk.

The courts were meant to protect the people, not serve a wannabe
authoritarian. But if Trump gets his way, justice will only serve those in
power, while everyone else pays the price.

We can’t let that happen. Demand Justice PAC is fighting to root out
Trump’s corruption in our courts and ensure they stand for justice, the
law, and the people — not for one president’s ego.

body:
There are more primary elections just around the corner.
# [](https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/892?refcode=em20260318-6023-footer&t=1&akid=6023%2E420207%2En0hygQ)
Peter,
$22 Million. Four primary races. AIPAC claimed victory in half of them.
**Even with all that money, AIPAC couldn’t stop progressives like Daniel Biss – a candidate I backed every step of the way. AIPAC dumped $7 million into defeating him, then added MILLIONS more, and _still_ got beat.**
[****](https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/47393?c0=pj-em-20260318-1.zFIeSH&refcode=em20260318-6023&t=2&akid=6023%2E420207%2En0hygQ)
AIPAC’s influence and the aggressive Republican dark money spending do swing elections, but the results in Daniel’s race prove that people power is stronger.
When we show up and go all out to support progressive candidates, _we can win._
And Peter, the midterms are just getting started. More primary races are heating up, and you can bet AIPAC will continue spending HUGE sums to defeat progressive candidates daring to speak up for working people and oppose Trump’s war in Iran.
**We need to back progressive candidates who fight for justice, stand up to AIPAC, and support working families — but it’s impossible without grassroots donors like you.**

subject: How it all started
body:
| | Peter –

Four years ago, with a baby in my arms and a shop to run, I decided I couldn’t sit back while politicians ignored Southwest Washington. So I decided to roll up my sleeves and take matters into my own hands.

The work that followed has been some of the toughest and most rewarding I’ve ever faced.

Nancy Mace wasn’t born into power. She worked for every inch of ground she’s gained.

**_Frankie Muse Freeman. Maya Angelou. Ora Lee Malone. Josephine Baker._**

Peter, what do these women all have in common? **If you guessed they all share roots in St. Louis, you'd be right!**

**Frankie Muse Freeman** served as an Assistant Attorney General for her state and later became the first woman appointed to the U.S. Commission on Civil Rights.

**Maya Angelou** , the beloved poet, author, and activist, told the world why the caged bird sings. She worked alongside Martin Luther King Jr. and Malcolm X and used her words to inspire generations.

**Ora Lee Malone** , a trailblazer in the labor movement, organized a garment factory union made up largely of Black workers. Today, she's recognized as one of the first leaders to connect the fight for racial and gender equality with the broader movement for working-class economic justice.

**Josephine Baker** , an international icon of music and dance, used her fame to fight segregation. She was the only official female speaker at the 1963 March on Washington and refused to perform for segregated audiences, even protesting discriminatory venues like the New York Stork Club.

This Women's History Month, we're celebrating the incredible Black women who helped shape our city's story and pushed our country forward.

At a time when the Trump administration is working overtime to erase the contributions of Black women across the country, Wesley is proud to stand up for the truth. In Congress, he has pushed back against attacks on voting rights that disproportionately affect Black communities and spoken out to defend Black history museums and institutions. But protecting and honoring the legacy of Black women is a responsibility that belongs to all of us.

Peter ,
Donald Trump fired Kristi Noem, but his new pick to lead the Department of Homeland Security, Sen. Markwayne Mullin, may be even worse.
When asked point-blank during his confirmation hearing whether the administration would send ICE agents to patrol polling places, he refused to rule it out.
What would that look like in November?
* Federal agents hovering near voting locations
* Legal voters second-guessing whether showing up is worth the risk
* A government that knows fear changes turnout
This is how voter suppression on a massive scale works. They’re pushing laws to make voting harder, reviving conspiracy theories about elections that have already been debunked, and leaving the door open to sending enforcement agencies anywhere they want.
This is coordinated, but it only works if nobody pushes back.
That’s where we come in. GOTV PAC is working on turnout operations designed for exactly this kind of environment, meeting voters where they are, making sure they know their rights, and getting them to the polls anyway.
If you’re able, chip in to help us scale that work right now. [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/gotvpac2026?refcode=em03182026]

I’m going to say what too many politicians won’t: What’s happening in Washington isn’t normal — and it’s hurting families here at home.
While Coloradans are worrying about grocery bills, healthcare costs, and whether they’ll ever be able to retire with dignity, our representative is busy chasing outrage, breaking rules, and embarrassing this district on a national stage.
Lauren Boebert calls it “fighting.” I call it failing — failing to show up for rural communities, to deliver for small businesses, and to understand how hard life has gotten for working families.
It’s time for a change. That’s why I’m running to defeat Lauren Boebert.
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/trisha-dsg-email? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/trisha-dsg-email?]
I’m Trisha Calvarese. I grew up here, I went to public schools here, and when my parents were both battling cancer at the same time, I came home to take care of them.
I’ve spent my career fighting for working people — from representing 12.5 million union members to helping secure historic investments in American manufacturing, clean energy, and innovation that are creating good-paying jobs right here in Colorado.
I know what serious leadership looks like. And every day, Lauren Boebert chooses headlines over hard work and stunts over solutions.
Washington insiders are betting she can keep getting away with it. But they’re wrong. This race is winnable. It can flip the House and send a message that Colorado won’t tolerate another term of chaos, cruelty, and incompetence.
But only if we fight back — together. So if you’re ready for a hometown candidate who shows up, tells the truth, and puts working families first, I’m asking you to chip in $10, $25, or whatever you can right now. [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/trisha-dsg-email?]

body:
Our redistricting fight is gaining headlines across Virginia and beyond, and all eyes are on the Commonwealth right now.
# [](https://act.virginiansforfairelections.com/go/629?refcode=em20260318-350&t=1&akid=350%2E12592%2EndQz5h)
Our redistricting fight is gaining headlines across Virginia and beyond, and all eyes are on the Commonwealth right now. Just take a look at this headline in _The Hill_ :
[](https://act.virginiansforfairelections.com/go/41?c0=em_ms_vafe_20260318_2.bZq-He&amount=3&refcode=20260318-350&t=2&akid=350%2E12592%2EndQz5h)
Early voting is underway, and on April 21 Virginians will vote to protect our democracy from blatant partisan power grabs.
The amendment is simple: _it requires voter approval of congressional maps ahead of midterms._ That means politicians can’t redraw districts in the dark. That means Trump and his MAGA allies can’t rig elections in their favor behind closed doors.
But this vote is coming fast. MAGA groups are pouring millions of dollars into Virginia right now to misinform voters and organize support for a NO vote.
Don’t forget a dark money group just sent out mailers trying to compare the redistricting amendment on the ballot to Jim Crow, while using imagery of segregation and the KKK.
What voters hear in the final days could decide everything. That’s why we’re organizing urgently to cut through the noise and:
* **Educate voters** on what the amendment does
* **Counter MAGA misinformation** and deceptive talking points
* **Push back on big dark money spending** meant to tip the scales
* **Reach voters where they are** before April 21 and secure the YES vote

Former President Obama recently endorsed our YES campaign, and warned that Republican-controlled states have redistricted “to give themselves an unfair advantage in the midterms” and that “Virginians can respond.” _We agree._ But responding takes resources, and turnout will decide everything.
[**Every dollar counts****. Will you chip in $10, $25, or whatever you can today to help us reach voters across Virginia in this high-stakes election?**](https://act.virginiansforfairelections.com/go/41?c0=em_ms_vafe_20260318_2.bZq-He&amount=3&refcode=20260318-350&t=3&akid=350%2E12592%2EndQz5h)

Peter, It is March in Texas, which means two things: all eyes are on the 13 different Texas men and women's teams playing in the NCAA's March Madness tournament and everyone is filling out their bracket. But before you finalize that bracket, there is something you need to know. GlobalX Airlines holds the NCAA's March Madness charter contract. **They also run 73% of all ICE deportation flights in this country. ** The same company flying our favorite teams to the tournament deported over 1,600 students last year, many of whom were paying the exact same university fees that fund the GlobalX charter contract in the first place. Today, we are joining a coalition of national organizations to demand the NCAA drop GlobalX before the first game tips off. We have a letter ready to go to Athletic Directors, Chancellors, and NCAA leadership. Over 850,000 people have already signed and we are pushing to hit one million signatures while every sports desk in the country has their eyes on the tournament. It takes about 60 seconds to add your name.
---
[ **SIGN THE LETTER** ](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.qUXRBnqZ7T8nxbpAcIVwoUsWLkUMWlo_0JmZttSlm380d8MN-giZCIhORa_SSwja1fUc-qxvb7b6EU2G6BNghZhvOxIHJi1yRmFVru9KZf8fwYD0uf7Qxf32G-8VknyUIzecPkL50WtACjCuaJAXsn0AwcGMZXTq80Qau2k7nU8wOYO9WfBITVcfoP-Vmeqr_SzIn2rpEZ4MPAZQ8J6DiuUWAACnpIlorAR9K3XcokE2booGL6O2W1FncaqdSdVC1Y0yoX73mIqMvvbp-AA9Xeq4ItqPkwR3f8pEbwg2aoZK32uzI4c6oCVfUdCMxUBZuJ_nmXltjDUPokgdiCyTav4rYh6UCltfRc5jhg7yMw1TNOkAp7B77Yyd--4nenhUXbWeBw4vpREfj4N-OopETFd4aPr6KOB1BTXSID93EBdrqRZDeG7wn6g-ZOhaagN-U9Cr8ydxp-L4Ges30U01FnuHEAfZ8vO5nZdiztJMPhq7_0OeFDUbgPqFmy1o9qdOaN8GsCuosq37sEl_nTLc1VJbW1rXBMi6qwPX1u7QjdU/4p1/V4rLLOlXQmOqSHVyEmM7Cg/h1/h001.z-XX7U2_aD5SBpXujrujc0yTeiKRaF0kR8836EZbMvY)
---
Texas has a particular stake in this. Last year was the deadliest year in ICE detention in two decades and nearly a quarter of those deaths occurred right here in Texas. The country's largest ICE detention center sits at Fort Bliss in El Paso, people keep dying in there, and the investigations keep going nowhere. The Dallas ICE field office is one of the most active in the country and our public universities carry some of the largest international and DACA student populations anywhere. **As Texans we must be loud about what is happening in our own backyard even when the tournament is on. Especially when the tournament is on, because right now every camera in college sports is pointed at us.** The universities know what GlobalX is. They are just hoping nobody pays attention during the tournament. Let's make sure that does not happen.

clean_body: | | Peter, It is March in Texas, which means two things: all eyes are on the 13 different Texas men and women's teams playing in the NCAA's March Madness tournament and everyone is filling out their bracket. But before you finalize that bracket, there is something you need to know. GlobalX Airlines holds the NCAA's March Madness charter contract. They also run 73% of all ICE deportation flights in this country. The same company flying our favorite teams to the tournament deported over 1,600 students last year, many of whom were paying the exact same university fees that fund the GlobalX charter contract in the first place. Today, we are joining a coalition of national organizations to demand the NCAA drop GlobalX before the first game tips off. We have a letter ready to go to Athletic Directors, Chancellors, and NCAA leadership. Over 850,000 people have already signed and we are pushing to hit one million signatures while every sports desk in the country has their eyes on the tournament. It takes about 60 seconds to add your name. Texas has a particular stake in this. Last year was the deadliest year in ICE detention in two decades and nearly a quarter of those deaths occurred right here in Texas. The country's largest ICE detention center sits at Fort Bliss in El Paso, people keep dying in there, and the investigations keep going nowhere. The Dallas ICE field office is one of the most active in the country and our public universities carry some of the largest international and DACA student populations anywhere. As Texans we must be loud about what is happening in our own backyard even when the tournament is on. Especially when the tournament is on, because right now every camera in college sports is pointed at us. The universities know what GlobalX is. They are just hoping nobody pays attention during the tournament. Let's make sure that does not happen.
